tracks.narration: What can you build with just two arrows and a pair of dials?
Pick two arrows v one and v two. A linear combination is a v one plus b v two, where a and b are any two real numbers. That formula is the recipe.
Fix b at zero and sweep the dial for a. The output point slides along a single line through the origin — the line of every multiple of v one.
Now turn both dials at once. The point wanders all over the plane. Every reachable spot is some recipe a v one plus b v two — that whole region is the span.
Linear combinations are how you turn arrows into reach. Two dials, two arrows, the whole plane.
